So, wow, this hasn't been touched on in a while. I really enjoy the orientation files and I finally got to this one and I enjoyed it for the most part. I can't really neg on it for anything that anyone hasn't said already. It doesn't flow well, the author's already stated he didn't really seem to like it himself.

Actually, reading everyone else's comments, and now considering what I was going to say myself, I have to say the biggest blemish on this seems to be the lack of backstory or continuation, or both.

The biggest question I have now after meeting Carter and Marshall, is, obviously, who is Dark? Have you answered that. Does he or it have something to do with the scars on the "employees" heads?

item.title: (no title)
item.content:encoded:
Okay. The content of this Tale is not bad. But it's missing several elements that I feel would turn it into a more complete story.

First, the good:
- I liked the tone and the Orientation motif.
- I could understand what was going on.
- The descriptions of Marshall and especially Carter were cool.
- The scar-people were slightly interesting window-dressing.
- Description of Smalls slowly filing out of the room by himself was cute.

Now, the bad:
- Who is this Agent Smalls, and why should I care about him? Other than as a symbol of the fact that Foundation Agents can be bribed, I know nothing about him. What does he want? What did they offer him that made him willing to defect? Why is he so nervous?

- Much of the content of the Orientation kind of goes without saying. (Really? He's not allowed to admit he works with Marshall, Carter, and Dark? I didn't see that one coming.)

- Some juicy details like what this "punishment" actually entails, or hints that they might have ways of knowing about betrayal even without observing you, would have been great elements to add here. Imply, to the employees, that MC&D is already using skips to control its employees. Whether they're bluffing about it or not.

- Is this going anywhere? This is just part one of a bigger Tale about betrayal and then maybe some other things like redemption or revenge or intimidation, right?

- Why not show us how they got to Agent Smalls? That's the meat of the story being implied, here. How they got to him and what his Acquisitions are going to be. As a Sleeper Agent in the Field, he probably can't do much more than pass them intel about his assignments and maybe offer MC&D first dibs on any skips he finds in the field. All of that could be touched upon if not outright explored, if you're looking to stretch this out a few pages.

- I'm sorry, but I don't know who Jenkins was. I don't get the joke. Like, I get it from context, I know why Carter and Marshall think it's funny, but it's not funny to me because I'm not in on the joke. There may be no graceful solution to this problem other than linking to whatever Tale or SCP first introduced Jenkins. Perhaps in a footnote.

Good luck, I look forward to seeing where you go with this. :)

item.title: (no title)
item.content:encoded:
The introduction is neutral-vote territory. It just doesn't do anything.

I downvoted in the second half. We get stuff like,

one that belied an immense and inhuman intelligence.

His chuckle was cold and knowing.

Like, this is not even trying. It is stuffing bricks with characterization and then chucking those bricks at your face. Shit hurts, man, now I got a concussion.

And the image of

The empty sound of wheezing laughter filled the room.

it's just so cliche I don't even know how to respond to it. It's so immensely shorthand for "these guys are evil" that it's like you can't be bothered to show them doing evil things or being evil people so instead you give them a wheezing voice and make them old and scheming and then you have them ALL GIVE AN EVIL LAUGH.

so yeah, -1'ed.
